terms.definition: Non-target species or undersized fish caught and usually discarded.
terms.examiner: Reduced by mesh size and shape, escape panels and acoustic deterrents.

terms.definition: Catching fish faster than the population can replace them.
terms.examiner: Signs: falling catch per unit effort and smaller, younger fish.

terms.definition: A limit on the mass of a species that may be landed.
terms.examiner: Can lead to discards if fish over the quota are thrown back dead.

terms.definition: An area where no fishing is allowed.
terms.examiner: Protects breeding stock; fish spill over into surrounding fished areas.

terms.definition: Farming aquatic organisms such as fish, shellfish and seaweed.
terms.examiner: Extensive systems have low inputs and stocking density; intensive systems have high.

terms.definition: Living on or near the sea bed.
terms.examiner: Caught by trawling, which damages the sea bed; pelagic fish live in open water.

terms.definition: Farming several species together so that the wastes of one are used by another.
terms.examiner: Reduces pollution and raises total yield.
